chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from one not specified from Abu al-Maghra', and Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about the sacrifice of the Murji'ah and the Haruriyyah, so he said: Eat and be content and settle down until it becomes a matter of time, and it is possible that the report is specific to the state of necessity, according to what the report included which we presented earlier in the first chapter from his saying: 'I forbid you from the sacrifice of everyone who is upon a difference from what you are upon and your companions, except in the time of necessity.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat the meat sacrificed by the Murji'ah and Haruriyyah sects?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Shaykh al-Tusi records that Imam al-Sadiq (AS) permits consuming the sacrifices of the Murji'ah and Haruriyyah, clarifying that the general prohibition is lifted specifically during times of necessity (*darurah*). This ruling is grounded in the report of Zakariyya ibn Adam, which explicitly excepts the state of need from the ban on eating their meat, reflecting the Shia jurisprudential principle of pragmatic permissibility when facing scarcity or requirement.
